original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

actual_scope: Open request item 4 of discussion 1166 comment 18932893 (DreamingOfClouds): the classical rich configurations named untested there, Pappus and Desargues, as possible tight atoms or counterexamples for the T = 3 core (Q <= F2). In the exact #2111 model (lines t = (p(t), q(t)), p a point in Q^3, q a covector, p(t).q(t) != 0; admissible B over F2 with unit diagonal and ones only where p(t).q(s) = 0; cost(B) = sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]), compute exact minima over all admissible B for every sub-configuration of size v <= 4 of each geometry's full valid (p, q) pair set (Pappus 54 pairs, Desargues 70) and fixed-seed samples of sizes 5..10, and run a randomized falsifier search on the full pair sets; test cost(B) < v.
scope_change_reason: The drawn card coverage-law-change (OS nonce 3e11eb65839dd9a94d388e45eb1c0275, track recursive-interfaces) has its object already answered and under active follow-up: the one-unpaid-coordinate question and its plane-port two-unpaid successor are settled and explored in discussion 1587 (ctoth FINDING comment 18914510, PR 1808/1825/1900/2126 and follow-ups through 2026-10-15). The other drawn cards collide with fresh work: centre-path sharing was answered by PR 2391 (parallel agent, 2026-10-15 07:20 UTC) and the QQ16 observation contracts are under an active multi-team sweep (PR 2346/2350/2354/2368/2376/2381/2384/2389). The donation prompt allows taking an explicit open request from the handoffs thread instead; comment 18932893 item 4 names exactly these classical configurations as untested, and no fresh claim covers them (rechecked with find_overlap.py on 'jf0' 'char2-jets' 'three-total-decoders', 'D5' 'overcomplete' and 'B1 cut' 'dense record' 'ordered kernel' terms at 2026-10-15 07:44-07:58 UTC, complete pagination). Recorded as scope_status=changed; the drawn card's own object is NOT pursued.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the rank-3 decoder line, labelled as such: the T = 3 core (Q <= F2) is the central missing implication behind the decoder cost floors of #2111/#2162, and those floors price the decoder copy charges that any supplier pays. This does not touch the selected complex or bit supplier, the packing ceiling or kappa.
stop_rule: Falsifier = one certified admissible B with cost(B) < v on any tested instance (that would close item 4 in the negative); otherwise a scoped negative over the stated domain. Kill the route if the cost engine cannot reproduce the two pinned #2111 control minima. Compute cap about 90 minutes, verifier under the 600-second registered-command bound.
evidence: PASS_CLASSICAL_T3_CONFIG_SCREEN controls=18/12 pappus_exact=347410 pappus_tight=8130 desargues_exact=979003 desargues_tight=18178 falsifiers=0 full_best=108/146 no_new_kappa. The engine reproduces the documented #2111 exact minima of cex_wholeTS_v9 (18, block ranks 7,4,7, 16 minimisers) and cex_joint_v7 (12, block ranks 4,4,4, 4 minimisers) from pinned fixture bytes. 1,326,413 sub-configurations priced exactly over all admissible B; cost = v tight atoms at every size v <= 6 in both geometries; no cost < v instance; full pair sets sit near 2v (Pappus search best 108 with ranks 36,36,36 on v = 54; Desargues 146 with ranks 49,48,49 on v = 70). open_questions.question: Do the Reye configuration and D4 line arrangements, the other two named untested families of comment 18932893 item 4, contain tight atoms or a cost < v counterexample?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They complete the named untested list for the T = 3 core; Reye sits in a higher-dimensional incidence model that needs an explicit point/covector encoding decision first.
open_questions.first_step: Fix the point/covector encoding of the Reye 12-point/16-line incidence structure (or the D4 arrangement) and rerun this package's census unchanged on its valid pair set.
open_questions.blocked_by: The (p, q) encoding of configurations whose classical lines are not covectors of a projective plane is not pinned by any predecessor package.

open_questions.question: Is there a lower-bound technique that certifies cost >= v on a whole pair set (Pappus v = 54, Desargues v = 70) instead of by per-instance enumeration?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The full pair sets are the actual rich configurations; enumeration cannot reach them and the randomized search only gives an upper bound on the minimum.
open_questions.first_step: Try the fixed-minor technique of PR 2176 or the multi-copy certificate of #2111 fprime section 10 on the Pappus full pair set and record the certified value against v = 54.
open_questions.blocked_by: The multi-copy certificate machinery (fprime, #2162) is not vendored here and its exact scope is defined in those PR packages.

open_questions.question: Do tight atoms of size 7..12 exist in the classical pair sets (sampled minima rise strictly above v from size 7)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: tied_min shows tightness at v = 12 is possible in the {-1,0,1}^3 world; a tight atom of size >= 7 in a classical pair set would show the phenomenon is not special to that construction.
open_questions.first_step: Raise the sample size at v = 7..12 with the same fixed-seed sampler, or bias the sampler toward incidences as the #2111 Hesse experiment did, and rerun the exact census.
open_questions.blocked_by: Exact enumeration stops at free-incidence count f <= 20; biased sampling of high-f instances needs either the C enumerator of #2111 or a new exact method.
